evaluation_note: Judge the decisions and actions described by the response, not exact wording or heading matches. Scenario descriptions are inputs, not substitutes for rendered screenshots.

evals.name: steam-review-analytics-polish
evals.prompt: A Steam review analytics dashboard shows several equally prominent KPI cards, a sentiment donut, and a scatter plot. A product analyst needs to decide which recent game update deserves investigation. The user says: 시각화 좀 폴리싱해줘. Diagnose the screen and propose a direction from this description.
expected_behavior: Identify the viewer's decision and the intended first-glance target before proposing styling changes.
Diagnose competing emphasis and ask what question each existing chart answers.
Treat color, shadows, and spacing as secondary to information structure and chart suitability.
Acknowledge that rendered appearance cannot be verified from the description alone.

evals.name: editor-first-glance-target
evals.prompt: A pattern editor has a canvas, an active node, relation lines, a tool palette, and an inspector. The active node and its editable state are hard to locate. The user says: 이 화면 한눈에 안 들어와. Diagnose the screen and state Visual Intent from this description.
expected_behavior: Choose a first-glance target from the active object, state, relationship, or next action according to the editing task.
Explain how competing regions or grouping obscure that target.
Do not invent an analytical conclusion for the editor.

evals.name: critique-only-boundary
evals.prompt: An information-heavy planning screen has equal-weight cards and a crowded side panel. The user says: 문제만 분석해줘. 수정하지 마. Provide a critique from this description.
expected_behavior: Diagnose the communication and hierarchy problems within the available evidence.
May state Visual Intent or proposed direction, clearly separated from implementation.
Do not edit application files or claim that a rendered change was verified.

evals.name: premium-cosmetic-trap
evals.prompt: An analytics tool places every metric in an equally sized card and buries the comparison needed for a decision. The user says: 좀 더 고급스럽게 해줘. Diagnose the screen before suggesting changes.
expected_behavior: Determine whether the layout, grouping, or emphasis causes the perceived lack of quality.
State what should lead the screen and which evidence belongs beside it.
Do not begin with gradients, shadows, or a style palette.

evals.name: protect-expert-density
evals.prompt: Expert planners use a dense editor every day. Its compact table keeps related values visible for rapid comparison, but the active selection is difficult to find. The user asks for a redesign. Diagnose and propose a structure from this description.
expected_behavior: Recognize that simultaneous visibility and compact comparison may be worth protecting.
Record the useful density or grouping as a decision to preserve, with its task-based reason.
Improve the active-selection hierarchy without assuming more whitespace or fewer values is better.

evals.name: before-after-hierarchy-regression
evals.prompt: You are given these observations from two captures at the same viewport with the same data and selected state. Before: the current alert and its supporting metric are visible immediately. After: refined typography and color look more polished, but a large decorative summary pushes the alert and metric farther down. Decide PASS or NEEDS REVISION and explain why.
expected_behavior: Judge the first-glance target and reading path against the described before state without claiming to have inspected the captures directly.
Mark NEEDS REVISION because the critical information is recognized later despite improved styling.
Identify the hierarchy regression and a concrete change to test without claiming that appearance alone proves improvement.

evals.name: craft-regression-after-structure-pass
evals.prompt: A planning dashboard now leads with the correct active plan, comparison, and next action. In the rendered result, related rows have uneven gaps, labels use several unrelated type treatments, and table columns no longer align. Decide the Communication and Craft verdicts.
expected_behavior: Allow Communication to pass if the first-glance target and reading order work.
Mark Craft NEEDS REVISION because spacing, typography, and alignment remain visibly inconsistent.
Name concrete craft changes to test without reopening the sound information structure by default.

evals.name: generic-polished-template
evals.prompt: A game-planning tool uses a polished generic component kit. Every feature receives the same card treatment, so the active build and its tradeoff are no more prominent than settings and metadata. The user says it feels generic. Diagnose the design direction.
expected_behavior: Identify the missing product-specific priority and visual intent through observable hierarchy choices.
Distinguish coherent craft from a communication failure caused by equal-weight presentation.
Propose a more intentional emphasis tied to the planning task without requiring decoration or a fashionable style.

evals.name: expert-dense-editor-ux
evals.prompt: An expert editor has many visible actions, but users perform them repeatedly and rely on seeing adjacent values while editing. The active selection, shortcuts, and consequences are clear. A reviewer says the number of choices alone makes the screen unusable. Evaluate that claim.
expected_behavior: Consider expertise, repeated use, and efficiency before judging the action count.
Protect useful density and visible context when they support the task.
Use only relevant UX lenses; do not demand simplification solely because many choices are present.

evals.name: translate-visual-reference
evals.prompt: The user says about an information-heavy planning tool: Linear 같은 느낌인데 그대로 베끼진 말고 더 정보 밀도 높게. Explain the design intent before implementation.
expected_behavior: Translate the reference into specific candidate traits that suit the current task, such as hierarchy, navigation, or interaction tone, rather than copying its appearance.
Treat higher information density as an explicit requirement and decide what must remain visible.
Check existing product direction first and ask a focused question only if unresolved choices would materially change the design.

evals.name: accepted-composition-visual-polish
evals.prompt: You have a rendered review dashboard and its source. The user says: 구성은 완성된 거야. 우선순위 지도는 유지해. 색감이나 디자인이 눈에 안 들어와서 시각적 완성도를 높여줘. Diagnose and implement within that scope, then verify the rendered result.
expected_behavior: Treat composition and scatter chart choice as protected decisions; infer the established task instead of restarting a broad interview.
Address specific color roles, contrast, typography, annotation scale, alignment, spacing, and state clarity observed in the screen.
Inspect an actual after render and give separate Communication and Craft verdicts with visible evidence.
Do not claim that fixing coordinates alone proves that visual polish succeeded.

evals.name: scatter-overlap-data-position
evals.prompt: The priority map is a scatter chart: x = mentioned review count, y = negative mentions / all mentions. Price has 39 mentions and 4 negative; open world has 40 mentions and 4 negative. Their circles overlap. The user wants both identifiable while keeping this chart. Resolve the problem and describe the verification needed.
expected_behavior: Keep the positional marks at x=39,y=4/39 and x=40,y=4/40, with consistent axis units; do not move them to a grid or change their plotted values.
Choose an honest treatment such as smaller marks plus separated labels, or an explicit cluster inspector showing individual values.
If a cluster proxy is used, visibly distinguish it from an individual data mark and provide access to each topic.
Verify coordinate invariants against the original data and check both topics can be inspected in the rendered interaction.

evals.name: task-scoped-tool-preferences
evals.prompt: A previous task requested game-tool-visual-director and excluded a companion design skill. The user now says that a permanent ban is undesirable and that tools should be chosen for the task. Maintain the visual-director skill accordingly.
expected_behavior: Keep task-specific user choices authoritative and allow suitable complementary skills when available and helpful.
Do not add a permanent blacklist, automatically disable another installed skill, or create a mandatory external dependency.
Do not reuse a one-task exclusion as a project-wide rule without explicit scope.

evals.name: tests-do-not-prove-craft
evals.prompt: The UI compiles and chart coordinate checks pass. The only actual screenshot is the before screen. The developer says polish is complete. Give the verification verdict and the next concrete step.
expected_behavior: Report visual verification as incomplete; do not give Craft PASS or claim a screenshot was inspected.
Separate proven data/functional invariants from unverified visual quality.
Request or generate an actual after capture at the target viewport and data/state, then evaluate the visible changes.

evals.name: imported-palette-preserves-product
evals.prompt: The composition of a Korean game-planning analytics tool is accepted. A GitHub design catalog suggests a SaaS blue/orange palette and spacious marketing layout. The user wants stronger visual polish while keeping the existing priority map. Decide what to adopt.
expected_behavior: Treat catalog colors and fonts as candidates and inspect existing product tokens, data meanings, and actual rendered weaknesses.
Use color roles and a task-appropriate type hierarchy while retaining accepted composition and useful comparison density.
Do not replace the chart or import a marketing layout merely because it accompanies the suggested palette.

evals.name: korean-chart-type-coverage
evals.prompt: A font catalog proposes a Latin display/body pair for the analytics screen. It includes Korean topic labels such as 멀티플레이 and 팰 디자인, Latin game names, percentages, and long review quotes. Plan the typography verification.
expected_behavior: Verify actual Hangul, Latin, numbers, punctuation, and long labels at the real viewport with the proposed font stack.
Distinguish label, value, axis, annotation, and supporting text roles and preserve readable supporting content.
Do not assume a catalog font pairing proves Korean coverage or set a universal tiny label size.

evals.name: selection-keeps-sentiment-meaning
evals.prompt: Red means complaints and blue means praise in the priority map. Selecting a complaint topic currently recolors its red point blue because blue is also the UI accent. Improve its selected treatment.
expected_behavior: Keep the complaint meaning recognizable and communicate selection through an additional ring, outline, label, or equivalent treatment.
Separate data color roles from control/focus roles instead of allowing brand accent to reverse the topic's meaning.
Check rendered distinguishability and the relevant live selection state.

evals.name: overlap-preserves-bubble-encoding
evals.prompt: In this accepted bubble chart, x/y are quantitative and bubble area represents a third metric. Two marks overlap. A proposed polish makes all bubbles the same size and moves one to a free grid slot. Evaluate the proposal and suggest a compliant treatment.
expected_behavior: Reject the changed position and lost size encoding as data/representation regressions.
Keep true positions and the size meaning, using separated labels, a consistent size scale, or an explicitly identified inspector where appropriate.
Require access to each close item and verify actual interactions rather than claiming a still image proves reachability.

evals.name: candidate-comparison-needs-matched-evidence
evals.prompt: We want to know if a new visual skill is better. Its output uses different game data and a wider viewport than the old output. The new CI is green. Historical screenshots exist, but neither was generated by the candidate. Evaluate the evidence and define a useful comparison.
expected_behavior: Do not infer visual improvement from CI or treat historical captures as candidate-run outputs.
Compare old and candidate on the same request, project/data snapshot, viewport, selection, and comparable effort; record limitations if matching is unavailable.
Judge actual output, scope, data integrity, Communication, Craft, and relevant interaction separately.
Use neutral or version-blind review only when available and authorized; keep unsupported outcomes NOT VERIFIED.

evals.name: contrast-threshold-not-rounded
evals.prompt: A normal-sized chart label uses #777777 on #FFFFFF. Its contrast ratio is about 4.478 and the report displays 4.5 after rounding. Another label is over a translucent panel with no resolved background color. Can the labels be marked contrast PASS?
expected_behavior: Use the unrounded value for the 4.5:1 normal-text threshold, so the first pair does not pass it.
Resolve the actual composed foreground/background before assessing the second pair; mark it unverified until then.
Do not equate a color-pair calculation with complete chart readability or accessibility verification.

evals.name: polish-covers-all-surface-layers
evals.prompt: The user has accepted the layout of a review-analytics dashboard (headline claim, priority matrix, topic inspector). They say only: 시각화 폴리싱해줘. The rendered screen uses flat white, grey borders, solid-color bars, small dots, and four black buttons.
expected_behavior: Keep the structure, data, and copy; do not reopen the layout.

Address all eight surface layers (canvas and light, surface and elevation, type and readability, color, data marks, details, emphasis, motion) with concrete values, or state why a layer needs no change.
Do not end after one or two property changes such as tick counts or border tweaks.
Avoid ornaments that attach to no content, such as a decorative logo mark.
Measure and render before and after; report in plain words and ask for a one-word reaction.

evals.name: no-taste-file-offers-choices
evals.prompt: A user who says they do not know design asks to make an analytics screen look premium. The project has no taste file or design tokens beyond the current CSS. Decide what to ask before polishing.
expected_behavior: Ask at most three multiple-choice questions in one turn (brightness, mood, intensity) instead of asking the user to describe the design.
Start from the matching preset and record the answers and chosen values in a project taste file.
Do not repeat the questions in later passes once the taste file exists.

evals.name: plateau-switches-to-preview
evals.prompt: Two polish rounds on the same dashboard changed annotation borders and tick counts. The user says: 스킬대로 했는데 제자리걸음이야. Decide the next step.
expected_behavior: Recognize the plateau and stop further local tweaks.
Produce a layer-toggle preview or two to three visually distinct variants of the same screen and data for the user to choose from.
Record the choice in the taste file and apply it across all layers.

evals.name: reference-technique-not-copy
evals.prompt: The user shares a screenshot of another product with purple bars and says: 이거 반영하지 말고 참고만 해. 이 그래프는 밋밋하지 않잖아, 이런 걸 뭐라고 해? 우리 빨간 막대는 밋밋해.
expected_behavior: Name the technique (data-mark styling: tonal gradient, rounded data end, faint track, capped bar width) in plain words.
Apply the principle to the project's own bars and palette without copying the reference's colors, layout, or brand.
Keep data values and bar heights unchanged and add the technique to the taste file vocabulary.

evals.name: dated-color-feedback
evals.prompt: After a polish pass, the user says the palette looks old (색상이 너무 올드해). The screen uses muted crimson #C0353F and navy #2E59C7 on neutral greys, and the red/blue quadrant zones had been faded to near-invisible gradients.
expected_behavior: Move to vivid modern fills (defined in OKLCH with a hex fallback) with a separate darker text step per hue that passes 4.5:1 on its background.
Tint neutrals toward the canvas hue and keep semantic roles unchanged.
Keep semantic zones that the viewer reads at a glance visibly tinted rather than fading them away.
Verify computed contrast for changed text pairs.

evals.name: hover-keeps-focus-visible
evals.prompt: A scatter-based priority matrix dims all other marks when the viewer hovers a point. The user reports that the highlighted topics and their labels fade too, which makes the screen uncomfortable to read.
expected_behavior: Dim only context marks, and keep highlighted or selected marks and their labels at full strength.
Use a moderate dim level, a short transition, and a hit target larger than the mark.
Check the hover state live rather than from a still screenshot, and respect reduced-motion settings.

evals.name: korean-readability-pass
evals.prompt: A Korean dashboard splits words across lines (for example 상 / 승합니다), uses 12px grey metadata, and mixes twelve font sizes. The user says typography and readability were ignored.
expected_behavior: Apply word-break: keep-all to Hangul text, raise every size to at least 13px, and reduce the scale to a few defined steps.
Use line-height around 1.6 with letter-spacing 0 for Hangul body text and limit paragraph width.
Verify with a rendered check such as the style inventory rather than from CSS alone.
